title: Every Way to Find a Job in the UK, Ranked Worst to Best
description:
Every Way to Find a Job in the UK, Ranked Worst to Best


If you are stuck in the UK job search, firing off LinkedIn Easy Apply and Indeed applications and hearing nothing back, you are probably spending 90% of your time on one of the worst methods there is. In this video I rank every realistic way to find a job in the UK from worst to best, and show you why they all really come down to one thing: how warm you get before you apply.

Roughly 70% of jobs are never posted publicly. They get filled through referrals, internal networks and direct outreach before they ever reach a job board. These are the job search strategies that actually move you up the ranking, whether you are a career changer, a recent leaver, or just not getting interviews from the big boards.


What you'll learn in this video:
- Why auto apply bots and mass applying convert at just 1 to 3% and get you filtered out
- The applicant tracking system search trick that surfaces live roles days before the big boards
- How to make recruiters find you on LinkedIn by fixing one thing in your profile
- The 2 minute hiring manager outreach that gets 3 to 5 times the interview rate
- Why a referred candidate converts at 15 to 30% and how to get warm before you apply


VIDEO CHAPTERS:
0:00 The most popular way to find a job is the worst
0:33 Why this is one ranking, not seven methods
0:55 No. 7: Auto apply bots and Easy Apply spraying
1:04 No. 6: Mass applying on the big job boards
1:44 How Arun went from no replies to an offer in 3 weeks
2:08 No. 5: Recruiters and recruitment agencies
2:54 No. 4: Careers pages, niche boards and the ATS search trick
3:40 No. 3: Getting recruiters to find you on LinkedIn
4:29 No. 2: Direct outreach to the hiring manager
5:32 No. 1: The hidden job market and warm referrals
6:29 Who to actually contact and how to follow up
6:55 The one pattern behind the whole ranking


Most people pour all of their energy into the very bottom of this list and wonder why nothing comes back. If you want to climb it, this is where I would start.

WORK WITH ME:
Join my free community for the full job search system, the outreach templates, and the exact way to get warm before you apply:
https://community.offeraccelerator.co.uk/join?invitation_token=f1eaf2eb4891316c06b827f77255cb8b209dd952-daae48f6-0b4f-44fe-833a-04e7c487467c&utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=description&utm_campaign=every-way-find-job-uk-ranked


CONNECT WITH ME
LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/olivercordingley
Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/olivercordingley


WATCH NEXT:
1 In 3 Jobs You Apply To Are Ghost Jobs


ABOUT ME:
I dropped out of university at 19 to build recruitment software and ATS systems used by hiring teams. For years I spoke to hundreds of hiring managers and recruiters every day, learning exactly how candidates get filtered, shortlisted, and hired from the inside. I started coaching friends through their job search using what I'd seen, then raised investment, built a software company, and hired my own team. I've seen hiring from every angle.

Today I help job seekers land offers faster using a proven 3-step system. I've coached hundreds of candidates into roles at firms like JP Morgan, Goldman Sachs, Deloitte, EY, and PwC and many more.

transcript: If you're finding jobs by just firing off LinkedIn easy apply and indeed applications, you're using one of the worst methods on this entire list. Now, I've ranked every realistic way to find a job in the UK from worst to best. I'm going to show you the method that most people spend about 90% of their time on that sits right down near the bottom. Because the whole ranking really comes down to one thing. How warm are you before you apply? And how close you get to an actual human before your CV lands in just a rejection pile. So, the colder the method, the lower it ranks. So, let's start at the very bottom and then climb up. So, number seven at dead last is the auto apply tools. So, these are the bots and the browser extensions that fire your CV at 300 jobs overnight whilst you sleep. And on paper, it feels like a shortcut. It feels productive. Because in reality, most decent employers actively filter these out and you've just told their system that you have been the least targeted and the least interested applicant in the entire pile. You are not saving time. You're paving the way to get ignored faster. So, if you're running one of these, that's the first thing that you need to stop today. And they're actually pretty expensive, so cancel that subscription. So, number six is the one that you're probably living right now. It's mass applying cold on the big public job boards. That's your LinkedIn's, that's your Indeed's, your Total Jobs. And this is where most candidates put nearly all of their energy in. And a generic CV fired into a pile just converts at something like 1 to 2% and part of that is because a good chunk of those postings aren't even real live open jobs. But the bigger reason is simpler than that. You're a complete stranger competing against thousands of other complete strangers. And nobody in that company has a single reason to trust you yet. And I've watched this from the other side of the table. So, I built recruitment software. So, I've seen exactly what happens to those applications the second they land in the ATS. So, take a candidate for example I worked with recently called Arun. So, he was moving careers out of the NHS and when he first came to me, he said that he was doing the thing that most people are doing which is applying on LinkedIn and easy applying things like that. And he was getting nothing back. He was getting rejected. So, the moment he stopped spraying applications, he started climbing this exact ranking, he had an offer in under 3 weeks. So, watch out for what actually changes as we move up this list. Number five are recruiters and recruitment agencies. Now, this feels like a setup because you're finally talking to a real person whose entire job is placing people like you. And sometimes it genuinely is a step up, but here's what most candidates get wrong. Cold messaging random recruiters is low return because they get spammed all day long and most of their roles get filled through their own contacts before you even hear about them. And the version of this that works is really rare. You find the one specialist recruiter who places people in your exact field at your exact level, and you build a real relationship with them in that single person. They'll put you in front of the roles that never hit the job boards. And the specialist recruiters like that, their reply rates are something like 20 to 30%. So, that one good specialist recruiter where you build a relationship with them beats sort of any other work that you would do. So, number four is going direct, and this is where the ranking starts to genuinely turn up in your favor. So, these are company careers pages, and I have a little trick that almost nobody uses that I'm going to share with you. So, most companies they run their applications through an applicant tracking system. So, these are things like Greenhouse, Lever, and Workday. And what the talent acquisition team do before they post a job is they post it on that system before it even gets picked up by the big job boards. So, what you need to do is go into Google and you search the name of the system alongside the job title you want, and you'll surface those live roles days before the competition even know they exist. So, it's the same effort as scrolling Indeed, but you get roughly double the conversion rate because you're not drowning in the same crowd as everybody else. Now, number three, and this is the moment it flips from sort of you chasing jobs to jobs coming to you. And this is optimizing your LinkedIn so the recruiters can find you because recruiters search LinkedIn with something called LinkedIn Recruiter. And that is the software that helps them find candidates like you. And what they do is they find one job title, and they almost never look past the first page of results. So, if your profile is smeared across five different job titles, you are effectively invisible to them. So, pick one, put the exact title you actually want in your headline and in your about section, literally word-for-word. And if you optimize your profile for LinkedIn Recruiter, you're quietly going to start getting messaged instead of getting skipped. Now, it is slower than reaching out yourself, and yes, it is a bit passive, but it's real and once it's set up, it costs you nothing. And if you want to learn how to optimize your profile for LinkedIn Recruiter, then you can click the link in the description below. Now, number two is the direct outreach to the actual hiring manager. This is not the recruiter and this is not some sort of portal where you submit your job application. This is the specific person who owns the team that you want to join. So, what you do is you find their email and instead of firing over yet another CV, you send them a two-minute video. That's who you are, how you found them, why you'd fit their team, and one small specific ask. And that approach consistently gets three to five times the interview rate of a normal application. And it works best at companies under 250 people where that manager actually controls their own hiring. And if you want to really stack those odds, then don't just send it in one way. You know, fire off that message on LinkedIn and by email at the same time, and then follow up with a quick call the next day. So, basically using those three touchpoints instead of just one. But, the whole thing still lives or dies on one rule. You lead with them, not with you. Because if you open by talking about yourself and what you want, they don't care. So, open with something specific about them or their company and make your ask answerable in one or two words. Because the shorter the answer you need, the easier it is for busy person to say yes. And then finally, number one, and the best way to find a job in the UK, and this is the one that actually nobody does properly, is you get warm before you even ever apply. Because roughly 72% of the jobs are never posted publicly at all. What they do is they get filled through referrals and internal networks before they even touch a job board. So, the entire game is getting a name behind your application before you send it. So, a referred candidate converts at something like 15 to 30% against 1 to 2% for a cold job blood application. And you didn't change your CV or your experience. You only changed that one thing, which is someone knows that you've applied in the company. Now, a team was a candidate I worked with and he had somebody already inside quietly put his name forward for a role that was never even advertised yet. So, by the time that he formally applied, he wasn't a stranger in a stack of PDFs. He was already someone that they actually spoken to. And that's the whole thing is that contact first, build the relationship, then the application. And the way that you do that isn't by messaging the CEO or the director. It's the people at your own level and it's probably either one step above. So, people at your level are the ones who you refer in and people one level up are the ones who actually hire you. So, you reach out and you have a genuine conversation and you ask for their read on the team and the role, not for the job. And make sure you follow up if they go quiet because silence isn't a no. It's just probably they're busy or they haven't seen their LinkedIn yet. So, look at that ranking one more time. Every single rung you climb, the same quiet thing is happening. You're getting warmer. You're getting closer to a real human before your CV ever lands. And the bottom of the list is you just shouting to strangers and trying to beg for jobs from employers. And the top is that you're walking in already known. And almost every candidate pours all of their energy and time into seven and six on this list. And then you wonder why nothing ever comes back. And Arun didn't do anything, you know, super ordinary. He just stopped applying cold and started applying warm and it took him a matter of weeks to get an offer. So, if you want the actual templates for the top of this list, the outreach messages, the way to build a proper target list, and the exact way to get warm before you apply, I put the whole system inside the offer accelerator and the link is in the description. So, come along and join and you'll know exactly how to walk into the interview room with confidence.
